headline: Chip-led rally caps Wall Street's best week since April 2025 as India slips on oil
subhead: The S&P 500 rose 1.6% and the Nasdaq 2.3% in Friday's half session and gold gained 3.8%, while the Nifty lost 277 points to 25,607.2 as Brent neared 98 dollars; India and some Asia and Europe prices on this page are still as of 26 Nov because the data feed has not updated.

us.text: The S&P 500 rose 1.6% to 7,297.5 and the Nasdaq 2.3% to 24,129.5 in Friday's half session, the S&P's best week since April 2025.
Micron gained 7.6% as memory, storage and optical chip makers led the rebound; Nvidia added only 0.8%.
Bond prices fell and the 10-year yield rose 1.8% to 4.94% as traders kept pricing a December Fed hike.

india.text: The Nifty fell 277.3 points to 25,607.2 and the Sensex 989 points on 27 Nov as Brent near 98 dollars and IT profit taking weighed.
FIIs net bought about Rs 1,634 crore on 27 Nov while DIIs net sold about Rs 556 crore, provisional exchange data show.
The rupee fell 60 paise to a provisional 92.98 per dollar on 27 Nov as crude rose after Houthi attacks on an Aramco facility.

global.text: On 27 Nov the Kospi gained 204 points to 4,915.7 and Samsung rose 4.6% after China's State Council pledged more market support.
Europe's STOXX 600 closed at 643.8 and the FTSE 100 at 10,698.8 on 27 Nov, led by chipmakers and miners.
Gold rose 3.8% to 3,668.5 dollars and silver 9.1% as metals bounced from 15-month lows on renewed Chinese buying.

weekly.narrative: Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO sparked a Monday surge and a Friday chip rebound finished the job, leaving the S&P 500 up 5.6% and the Nasdaq up 6.7% for the week, the S&P's best since April 2025, even as 3.3% core PCE inflation cemented bets on a December Fed hike. In India, the Nifty climbed toward 10-month highs on a long run of foreign buying before falling 277 points on Friday as Brent neared 98 dollars, ending four straight weekly gains. Gold rose 4.4% and silver 6.5% on the week after bouncing from 15-month lows, while bitcoin slipped 0.3% and stayed near 60,000 dollars amid heavy ETF outflows. Asian markets rallied on Friday after China's State Council pledged more capital market support. Next week turns on Sunday's OPEC+ meeting, US ISM data and November payrolls, and the RBI decision on 4 December, ahead of the Fed on 8 to 9 December.
